description:
Found by s501t (s505) probing F3 (Env): `my @o = ($PCLT_ONE, ...)` read the tied scalar's LATER value.  Pre-existing on main a33ce274.

Reproducer (perl prints `one 1 two`):
  require Tie::Scalar; tie my $s, 'Tie::StdScalar'; $s = "one";
  my @o = ($s, 1); $s = "two"; my @p = ($s); $s = "three"; print "@o @p\n";
PCL (main and the s501t tree): `three 1 three` -- the array keeps the proxy BOX, so every later read FETCHes again.  A list assignment copies VALUES (perl FETCHes once at the assignment).

=== DONE (s536a) === (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08; with #2601) -- the FIX SHAPE taken, array arm.
%p-array-store-scalar gains a tie-proxy arm beside the magic-cell arm: it stores the list assignment's own reading of a tied element, `(unbox (%p-tie-fetch item inner))` (the %p-assign-snapshot sibling), through the raw-value arms -- not the FETCH result BOX, which can be the tie object's own referent and carries ITS class (`$t = [7]; @r = ($t)` gave ref T2 when the box was passed on).  p-unshift / p-splice-impl PEEK at an item instead of unboxing it, so the store's FETCH is the only one (perl: one per copy; probed push / unshift / splice = 1 each).  Breaking cases probed identical: `@a = ($., $0 =~ ...)`, `$!` through unshift / splice.  The hash twin (%p-make-hash-entry) already copied the value (`{ k => $t }` probed = perl).  Guard Pl/t/tie-fetch-once-01.t rows 26-30 (perl lines), fail on 06a4b8ba.  Board: Text-CSV 76_magic.t row 12 (UNREDUCED #4183) passes.
Not changed: a FETCH that returns a BLESSED array / code ref loses the class in the copy, as the list-assignment sibling already does (the first-bless representation, #4061's family).
